syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Integration as an inverse process of differentiation

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that a function has a family of antiderivatives differing by a constant and fix the constant from a given condition.
Recall the standard indefinite integrals that follow from the derivatives of standard functions.
Use the sum and constant-multiple properties of indefinite integrals to integrate combinations of functions.

topics.title: Integration by substitution and trigonometric identities

concepts.learning_objective: Choose a suitable substitution to reduce an integral to a standard form.
Use trigonometric identities to rewrite integrands such as powers and products of sines and cosines.
Apply the standard integrals of 1/(x^2 ± a^2), 1/(a^2 - x^2) and their square-root forms.
Reduce integrals with a quadratic ax^2 + bx + c in the denominator to standard forms by completing the square.
Integrate (px + q)/(ax^2 + bx + c) by writing the numerator as A times the derivative of the denominator plus B.
Distinguish proper and improper rational functions and reduce improper ones by long division.
Write the correct partial fraction form for a proper rational function and integrate it.
Apply the integration by parts formula with a sensible choice of the first and second functions.
Use the result that the integral of e^x[f(x) + f'(x)] is e^x f(x) + C.
Apply the standard integrals of the square roots of x^2 + a^2, x^2 - a^2 and a^2 - x^2.

topics.title: Definite integral and the fundamental theorem of calculus

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the area function and use the first fundamental theorem to differentiate it.
Evaluate definite integrals as F(b) - F(a) using an antiderivative F.

topics.title: Evaluation of definite integrals by substitution

concepts.learning_objective: Change the limits of integration when a substitution is made and evaluate the new definite integral.
Use the properties of interchanging limits and splitting the interval of integration.
Apply the property that the integral of f(x) from 0 to a equals the integral of f(a - x) to evaluate integrals.
Use the properties of definite integrals of odd and even functions over a symmetric interval.

topics.title: Area under a curve using vertical strips

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the area under y = f(x) as the sum of thin vertical strips of area dA = y dx.
Calculate the area bounded by y = f(x), the x-axis and the ordinates x = a and x = b when f(x) is non-negative.
Calculate the area bounded by x = g(y), the y-axis and the lines y = c and y = d.
Decide whether vertical or horizontal strips describe a given region and set up the correct integral.

topics.title: Regions below the x-axis and curves crossing it

concepts.learning_objective: Take the absolute value of the definite integral when the curve lies below the x-axis.
Split the interval at the points where the curve crosses the x-axis and add the absolute areas of the parts.

topics.title: Areas of circles, ellipses and parabolic regions

concepts.learning_objective: Find the area enclosed by a circle x² + y² = a², or a quadrant of it, by integration.
Find the area enclosed by the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 by integration.
Use the symmetry of a circle, ellipse or parabola to reduce an area to one quadrant and multiply.
Recognise a differential equation and distinguish an ordinary differential equation from a partial one.
Find the order of a differential equation from its highest order derivative.
Find the degree of a differential equation when it is a polynomial in its derivatives, and recognise when it is not defined.
Verify by substitution that a given function is a solution of a differential equation.
Distinguish general and particular solutions and relate the number of arbitrary constants to the order.
Identify and solve first order, first degree equations whose variables can be separated.
Use a given condition or point on a curve to find a particular solution.
Model continuous growth with dP/dt = kP and interpret its solution.
Test whether a function of x and y is homogeneous and find its degree.
Solve a homogeneous differential equation using the substitution y = vx.
Write a first order linear equation in standard form and find its integrating factor.
Solve a first order linear differential equation using its integrating factor.

topics.title: Vectors: basic concepts, direction cosines and types

concepts.learning_objective: Find the direction cosines of a vector and use l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1.
Distinguish scalars from vectors and identify zero, unit, collinear, equal and negative vectors.
Add vectors geometrically using the triangle and parallelogram laws.
State and apply the commutative and associative properties of vector addition.

topics.title: Multiplication of a vector by a scalar and components

concepts.learning_objective: Find unit vectors and scalar multiples, and test collinearity using b = (lambda)a.
Perform vector operations using components along the unit vectors along the axes.

topics.title: Vector joining two points and section formula

concepts.learning_objective: Express the vector joining two points in component form and find its magnitude.
Find the position vector of a point dividing a segment internally or externally in a given ratio.
Compute the scalar product and use it to find angles and test perpendicularity.
Find the projection of one vector on another using (a . b)/|b|.
Compute the vector product and apply its properties such as anticommutativity.
Find areas of triangles and parallelograms using the magnitude of the vector product.

topics.title: Direction cosines and direction ratios of a line

concepts.learning_objective: Define the direction cosines of a directed line and use the identity l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1.
Convert a set of direction ratios of a line into its direction cosines.

topics.title: Direction cosines of a line through two points

concepts.learning_objective: Find the direction ratios and direction cosines of the line joining two given points.
Use proportional direction ratios to test whether three points are collinear.

topics.title: Equation of a line in space

concepts.learning_objective: Write and interpret the vector equation r = a + λb of a line through a point parallel to a vector.
Write the Cartesian form of a line and convert between the vector and Cartesian forms.
Find the acute angle between two lines from their direction ratios, direction cosines or equations.
Apply the conditions for two lines to be perpendicular or parallel.
Identify skew lines as lines in space that are neither parallel nor intersecting.
Compute the shortest distance between two skew lines using the vector formula.
Recognise parallel lines in space from proportional direction vectors and know they are coplanar.
Compute the distance between two parallel lines using d = |b × (a2 − a1)| / |b|.

topics.title: Linear programming problems and their terms

concepts.learning_objective: Describe a linear programming problem and the meaning of the words linear and programming in it.
Identify a linear objective function Z = ax + by and its decision variables.
Recognise linear constraints and the non-negative restrictions x >= 0, y >= 0.

topics.title: Mathematical formulation of a linear programming problem

concepts.learning_objective: Translate the limits stated in a real-life problem into linear inequalities in the decision variables.
Write the linear objective function to be maximised or minimised from the data of a problem.

topics.title: Feasible region, feasible solutions and the fundamental theorems

concepts.learning_objective: Determine the feasible region, its corner points and whether a point is a feasible or an infeasible solution.
Distinguish a bounded feasible region from an unbounded one.
Apply the theorems that place optimal values of a linear objective function at corner points of the feasible region.

topics.title: Corner point method on bounded regions

concepts.learning_objective: Solve a linear programming problem with a bounded feasible region by evaluating Z at its corner points.
Recognise that when two corner points give the same optimal value, every point of the segment joining them is optimal.

topics.title: Unbounded regions and problems with no feasible solution

concepts.learning_objective: Use the open half-plane test to decide whether the smallest or largest corner value is the optimum on an unbounded region.
Recognise a system of constraints that has no feasible region and hence no feasible solution.
Define and compute the conditional probability P(E|F) = P(E ∩ F)/P(F) for events of a finite sample space.
Apply P(S|F) = P(F|F) = 1, the addition property for P((A ∪ B)|F) and P(E′|F) = 1 − P(E|F).
Use P(E ∩ F) = P(E) P(F|E) = P(F) P(E|F), and its extension to three events, to find probabilities of successive events.
Test and use independence of events through P(E ∩ F) = P(E) P(F).
Distinguish independent events from mutually exclusive events.

topics.title: Partition of a sample space and theorem of total probability

concepts.learning_objective: Identify when a set of events forms a partition of a sample space.
Find the probability of an event using the theorem of total probability over a partition.
Apply Bayes' theorem to find the reverse probability of a cause given an observed event.
